rationale: naf-claude-agentic: val_n=214, naf_n_freqs=8, naf_hidden=128, naf_layers=4, naf_n_iter=3000, naf_lr=0.01, naf_tv_weight=0.0001, naf_n_clip=0.05, naf_outer_wall_s=1080, naf_per_scene_s=5.0, seed=42, rationale=ITER-1 feasibility (search-20260619-01, corrected protocol). GOAL: does naf (Neural Attenuation Field, per-scene self-supervised INR -- one coordinate-MLP optimized PER L277 slice against its OWN sinogram, no training set) run on Mayo under the corrected path (staged_canonical v3 mayo_ldct_fitted geometry, inlined single-val-ps probe -> reconstructs at L277 native ps ~0.73979, bg_target=truth) and produce a FINITE val_score + comparison.png within the HARD 20-min budget, scoring ALL 214 L277 slices under the 321px detector-geometry FOV (evaluate_calibrated default for AGENT4CT_DATASET=mayo_ldct_2d; no fov= override)? BUDGET REASONING (the load-bearing decision): NAF has NO training (train_n=0); the ENTIRE budget is the per-scene fit loop, total = val_n x per_scene. val=ALL 214 L277 slices is MANDATORY (protocol; do NOT reduce). 18-min outer wall (naf_outer_wall_s=1080, inside the 20-min compute budget, leaving headroom for the figure+IO before the 30-min sbatch kill) / 214 scenes = naf_per_scene_s=5.0 s/scene. Mayo is 512x512 images at 2304 views x 736 channels, so each Adam step = a 512^2 MLP forward + a 2304-view fan-beam forward-project + backward = EXPENSIVE; 5 s/scene buys only a handful of steps (a NeRF-style fit wants hundreds-to-thousands). naf_n_iter=3000 is a HIGH CAP so the PER-SCENE WALL (t_limit in fit_one_scene), NOT the iter count, is the governor -- each scene runs as many steps as fit in 5 s. To squeeze the most out of the tiny budget: leaner MLP than default (hidden 192->128, layers 5->4, n_freqs 10->8 => cheaper steps => a few more fit per scene) and naf_lr 5e-3->1e-2 (with only a handful of steps, a higher lr converges faster from the water-mu init). naf_n_clip=0.05 (sigmoid head out_scale), naf_tv_weight=1e-4 defaults. HYPOTHESIS: NAF is STRUCTURALLY FBP-bounded on dense rebinned Mayo (wrong inductive bias for dense-view CT -- solver_plan.md flags NAF/R2G hr~0 on dense-view; the discarded boundary-slice run hinted naf 0.911 < LD-FBP ~0.81-cal baseline, a behavior hint only) AND it is BUDGET-STARVED on the 214-slice protocol (5 s/scene = far too few per-scene Adam steps for a NeRF-style convergence). Expect val_ssim that does NOT clear the LD-FBP baseline (hr near 0). This iter ESTABLISHES that datapoint under the corrected metric -- a real finding (do NOT reduce val_n below 214 to make NAF look better). iter-2+ will tune ONE knob (per-scene step budget vs MLP capacity vs lr) but NAF cannot escape its structural ceiling on this dense substrate within a 20-min/214-scene budget.
